title: One question, many sources — the anchor
text: "What's our policy on contractor onboarding, and is there a prior decision already on file?" Answering that means reaching into the company's own knowledge, chat, drives, tickets, wikis, not the open web. The easy assumption, run one search and

title: A snippet, not an answer
text: The top result already has the answer. But a search result is a snippet, about 35 words, just enough to judge whether a document is worth opening. It was never built to answer anything by itself. The loop runs in three steps. Search returns

title: Search, read, feedback — the loop
text: Ranked snippets across every connected source. Read fetches the full text of the documents that matter using the ID from search. Feedback upvote what you used, downvote what you rejected, trains the ranker, and it happens before the task is called done. Two bundled scripts handle the busy work, one for searching with pagination, one for reading up to 50 documents at a time. Two rules keep

title: Design rules — index first, cursor pagination, empty-results logic
text: It honest. Always search the shared index first. It already ranks across every source, deduplicates, and respects permissions before falling back to one connector directly. And pagination is cursor-based. Pass the cursor back exactly as given, never build one yourself, stop when there isn't one. One catch, an empty result can mean two different things. title: The anchor returns — snippet, document, feedback
text: Onboarding question, search turns up a snippet that mentions a policy. That's step one. Reading the full document is what actually surfaces the exception buried in the next paragraph. Marking that document as used is step three, and it's what makes tomorrow's search better.

title: Both directions — found isn't complete, empty isn't proof
text: Finding something doesn't mean you have the whole picture. Some sources might not be connected yet. And finding nothing doesn't mean the answer doesn't exist. It might be a permissions gap, or a query that needs to broaden before you conclude that. Enterprise search isn't

title: Carry-out
text: One lookup. It's search for candidates, read the document that matters, then say what you used so the next search ranks better.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn. Here's the prompt. Read it with me. Search our internal docs for our policy on contractor onboarding. Read the full document, not just the snippet, and tell me if there's a prior decision on file. Then tell me what you used to answer before you finish. Liam in for Bear.
